unit_description: This unit focuses on telling time and elapsed time. Students read analog clocks to the nearest minute, match analog, digital, and written times, estimate time intervals in minutes, and find elapsed time and ending time.
unit_goals: Read analog clocks to the nearest minute.
Match analog, digital, and written times.
Find elapsed time and ending time.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students learn to read clocks precisely, match time formats, and solve elapsed-time problems.

lessons.lesson_title: Read Analog Clocks to the Nearest Minute
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by reading the hour and minute hands on an analog clock.
lessons.concept: An analog clock has an hour hand and a minute hand. The minute hand points to minutes, and the hour hand moves between hour numbers. Count by 5s for each large mark and by 1s for each small mark.
lessons.practice: Read analog clocks to the nearest minute.
lessons.objective: Read analog clocks to the nearest minute.

questions.prompt: How many minutes are between each large number on a clock?
The minute hand points to 3. How many minutes?
The hour hand is between 4 and 5. What hour is it?
questions.hint: The hour hand has not reached 5 yet.

learn.title: Read Analog Clocks to the Nearest Minute
teaching_points: The hour hand points to the hour or between hours.
Each small mark is 1 minute; each large number is 5 minutes.

example.prompt: What time is it when the hour hand is between 2 and 3 and the minute hand points to 7?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Read the time: hour hand between 5 and 6, minute hand on 9.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Read each analog clock to the nearest minute.

bigIdea.title: Read Analog Clocks to the Nearest Minute
bigIdea.subtitle: Use both hands
bigIdea.intro: An analog clock has two hands. The short hand tells the hour. The long hand tells the minutes. Count by 5s around the clock, then by 1s for the small marks.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why does the hour hand move between numbers?

ruleCards.description: The hour hand shows the current or last hour.

lessons.lesson_title: Match Analog, Digital, and Written Times
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by writing the same time in three ways.
lessons.concept: The same time can be shown on an analog clock, a digital clock, or written in words. 3:25 can be shown as 3:25 on a digital clock or as twenty-five minutes after three in words.
lessons.practice: Match analog, digital, and written times.
lessons.objective: Match analog, digital, and written times.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by matching time formats.

questions.prompt: What is half past 7 in digital form?

questions.hint: 45 minutes after 12 is a quarter to 1.

learn.title: Match Analog, Digital, and Written Times
teaching_points: Digital clocks show hours and minutes as numbers.
Written times use words like o'clock, quarter past, half past, quarter to.

example.equation: 2:40, twenty minutes before three, hour hand between 2 and 3, minute hand on 8

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Write 9:10 in words and draw it on an analog clock.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Match each time across analog, digital, and written forms.

flashcards.title: Time Formats
flashcards.instructions: Review analog, digital, and written times.

bigIdea.title: Match Analog, Digital, and Written Times
bigIdea.subtitle: The same time in different forms
bigIdea.intro: Time can be shown on an analog clock with hands, on a digital clock with numbers, or written out in words. All three forms represent the same moment.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How is 10:30 shown on an analog clock?

ruleCards.description: Hours and minutes written as numbers.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by guessing how many minutes common activities take.
lessons.concept: A minute is about the time it takes to walk around a classroom or sing a short song. Use real-life experience to estimate how long activities take in minutes.
lessons.practice: Estimate time intervals in minutes for daily activities.

questions.prompt: About how many minutes does it take to brush your teeth?
About how many minutes is a TV show?
About how many minutes does it take to eat lunch?

learn.title: Estimate Time Intervals in Minutes
teaching_points: Think about how long an activity usually takes.

example.prompt: Estimate how long it takes to walk to the bus stop.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Estimate how many minutes it takes to read a short story.
try_it.hint: A short story takes several minutes.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Estimate the number of minutes for each activity.

bigIdea.title: Estimate Time Intervals in Minutes
bigIdea.subtitle: Use what you know about time
bigIdea.intro: You can estimate how long things take by thinking about activities you already know. One minute is about the time it takes to sing the alphabet song or walk down the hall.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why is it helpful to estimate time in minutes?

ruleCards.description: One minute is enough time for a short task.
Think about how long similar activities take.

lessons.lesson_title: Find Elapsed Time and Ending Time
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting forward and backward by 5s and 10s on a clock.
lessons.concept: Elapsed time is the amount of time that passes from a start time to an end time. Count forward to find the ending time. Count backward to find the start time.
lessons.practice: Find elapsed time and ending time using number lines and clocks.
lessons.objective: Find elapsed time and ending time.

questions.prompt: A movie starts at 2:00 and ends at 3:30. How long is it?
questions.hint: From 2:00 to 3:30 is 1 hour and 30 minutes.

questions.prompt: A game starts at 4:15 and lasts 45 minutes. When does it end?
A bus ride ends at 7:20. It took 25 minutes. When did it start?

learn.title: Find Elapsed Time and Ending Time
teaching_points: Elapsed time = end time - start time.
Use a number line or clock to count minutes.
Break the time into easy chunks.

example.prompt: A party starts at 1:45 and lasts 1 hour and 20 minutes. When does it end?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A soccer practice starts at 3:30 and ends at 4:45. How long is it?
try_it.hint: From 3:30 to 4:30 is 60 minutes, plus 15 minutes.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Find the elapsed time or ending time for each problem.

bigIdea.title: Find Elapsed Time and Ending Time
bigIdea.subtitle: Count the minutes that pass
bigIdea.intro: Elapsed time is the time between a start and an end. Count forward to find when something ends. Count backward to find when it started. A number line can help.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How can a number line help find elapsed time?

ruleCards.description: Elapsed time is the time between start and end.
Add the elapsed time to the start time.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of reading analog clocks, matching time formats, estimating intervals, and elapsed time.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: reading analog clocks to the nearest minute, matching analog/digital/written times, estimating time intervals in minutes, and finding elapsed time and ending time.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about time and elapsed time.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: A show starts at 1:10 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it end?
What time is it when the minute hand points to 11 and the hour hand is between 8 and 9?

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: analog clocks + time formats + estimates + elapsed time = time

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A game starts at 3:15 and ends at 4:30. How long did it last?
try_it.hint: From 3:15 to 4:15 is 60 minutes, plus 15 minutes.

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 35 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 35 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Time
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: reading analog clocks to the nearest minute, matching analog, digital, and written times, estimating time intervals, and finding elapsed time and ending time.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about time and elapsed time?

ruleCards.description: Use both hands to tell time.
Find the time between start and end.
